free_text.inst.v2.D8: The record of my life is public to a fault, and I put a good deal of it there myself, some of it wrong on purpose. I was born in Hartford on the twelfth of May, 1907 - though for years I gave out my brother Tom's birthday, the eighth of November, because after he died in 1921 I could not stand to have a day of my own. Take the dates from the books, not from what I said at the time. What matters in it: Tom; my father and mother, who were the two best people I knew; Bryn Mawr; Luddy, whom I married in 1928 and used badly; the pictures; Spencer, for twenty-six years, which was not a settled married life and was never going to be; Fenwick, and the water. I did not want children and I did not have them, and I have never once regretted it. I worked, which is the whole of it.

notes: Birth-time provenance (A1-A3) genuinely undocumented in the biographical record - her birth DATE is itself a known muddle (born 12 May 1907; she publicly used 8 Nov 1907, her late brother Tom's birthday, for decades), so 'unknown' is the only defensible answer for the clock time. A8: no near-death before age eight is recorded; answered 'no' as absence-of-record rather than positive evidence. A9 'mixed': paternal grandfather Rev. S. S. Hepburn long-lived, but both maternal grandparents (Alfred and Caroline Houghton) died in 1892 in their forties, her mother orphaned as a teenager. A22 'significant': Howard Hughes's purchase of the film rights to The Philadelphia Story, made over to her, plus family property - not a conventional inheritance. A27 read as 'closest partnership' = Spencer Tracy (1942-1967): devoted but mixed - his marriage, his drinking, permanent concealment. A31 'brief': the withdrawn, sleepless years after Tom's suicide and the grief after Tracy's death are documented; no treatment for the mind is. A32 'none': she described herself plainly as an atheist with no religious or occult interest. A36 is unanswerable for her - she died 29 June 2003, so 'same' is a placeholder, not a finding. C2 'both': lifelong eye trouble dates from the fall into the Venice canal filming Summertime (1955) plus later cataract surgery, against otherwise serviceable sight. C6 answered 'gone well' on balance - her voice was her instrument for sixty years - but it is the weakest call here; the essential tremor from the late 1970s trembled head and voice and could as fairly be scored a difficulty. Part D (D1-D7) deliberately left unanswered: it asks about chapters of an astrological reading, and per the study rules no reading or verdict file was opened. D8 answered in her voice from biography only.
